subject: Math
subskill: Effect of Adding/Removing Data on Statistics
prompt:
[Figure 1]

The dot plot represents the $15$ values in data set P. Data set Q is created by adding $47$ to each of the values in data set P. Which of the following correctly compares the medians and the ranges of data sets P and Q?

choices.A: The median of data set Q is equal to the median of data set P, and the range of data set Q is equal to the range of data set P.
choices.B: The median of data set Q is equal to the median of data set P, and the range of data set Q is greater than the range of data set P.
choices.C: The median of data set Q is greater than the median of data set P, and the range of data set Q is equal to the range of data set P.
choices.D: The median of data set Q is greater than the median of data set P, and the range of data set Q is greater than the range of data set P.

explanation: Choice C is correct. The median of a data set with an odd number of values, in ascending order, is the middle value, and the range is the positive difference between the maximum and minimum values. Since data set P has $15$ values listed in ascending order in the dot plot, the median is the $8$th value. The cumulative counts are $1$, $3$, $6$, $10$, $15$, so the $8$th value falls within the value $19$. Therefore, the median of data set P is $19$. The maximum value is $22$ and the minimum value is $10$, so the range of data set P is $22 - 10$, or $12$. Data set Q is created by adding $47$ to each of the $15$ values in data set P. Adding $47$ to every value increases the median by $47$, making the median of data set Q $19 + 47$, or $66$. However, the range is unchanged because the maximum becomes $22 + 47$, or $69$, and the minimum becomes $10 + 47$, or $57$, giving a range of $69 - 57$, or $12$. Therefore, the median of data set Q is greater than the median of data set P, and the range of data set Q is equal to the range of data set P.
